Testimony of Representative Allison Hepler presenting
LD 1042, An Act to Require a Person Operating a Watercraft for
Recreational Purposes to Ensure All Passengers Under 13 Years of Age Wear
Coast Guard Approved Personal Flotation Devices
Before the Joint Standing Committee on Inland Fisheries and Wildlife

Good afternoon, Senator Baldacci, Representative Roberts and members of the Inland Fisheries
and Wildlife Committee. I am Allison Hepler, and I represent the towns of Arrowsic,
Georgetown, Phippsburg, West Bath and Woolwich. I am pleased to present LD 1042, An Act
to Require a Person Operating a Watercraft for Recreational Purposes to Ensure All
Passengers Under 13 Years of Age Wear Coast Guard Approved Personal Flotation
Devices.

As a member of this committee in 2022, I served on a stakeholder group to clarify aspects of a newly enacted boater safety law. In that stakeholder group, we tackled issues such as whether
persons of a certain age should be exempt from the boater safety and education course
requirement, how to handle differences between recreational and commercial boating, and how to ensure the safety of summer boat rentals. This committee enacted the recommendations of the
stakeholder group, and the recommendations were enacted by the 131" Legislature. Impoitantly, we kept the requirement that only people born after 1999 would be required to take a boater
safety and education course.
While the stakeholder group included members of the youth summer camp community, we did
not consider any changes to rules devoted to young people. However, a year ago a constituent
with a long history of teaching boater safety brought to my attention that state rules around
personal flotation devices (PFDS) worn by children differ from U.S. Coast Guard requirements.
Specifically, while current Maine statute is silent on a minimum age below which wearing a PFD
is required, rules of the Department of Inland Fisheries and Wildlife specify that children "age 10 and under" are required to wear a life jacket.

District 49: Arrowsic, Georgetown, Phippsburg, West Bath and Woolwich

This bill would put into statute a requirement that children who are under 13 be required to wear
a PFD, which is consistent with the Coast Guard requirement under 33 CFR 175.25.` As
indicated by Maine's recreational boater safety law, an exception to this requirement applies to
canoes owned by youth camps and log rafts subject to certain conditions. LD 1042 makes no
change to this part of the law.
I submitted this bill for a couple of reasons. First, I have great respect for Coast Guard rules. And, to be clear, Coast Guard law also allows for states to have different requirements from
federal rules. When states do have different requirements, the Coast Guard honors them.
However, changing Maine's age rules would make Maine consistent with the Coast Guard, and consistency would make for ease of enforcement.
Also, when contemplating changes to Maine law, I am a big fan of looking at what other states
do. On the BOATUS.org Website, there is a state-by-state listing of states and PF D requirements,
which will be provided to you.2 I decided to look at the 30 states that border the Atlantic, Pacific, Gulf and Great Lakes. Out of these 30, 19 state laws regarding children's requirements are
consistent with the Coast Guard. In New England, New Hampshire, Connecticut and Rhode
Island mirror the Coast Guard rules; Massachusetts is 11 and under. Maine's requirement at 10 and under is the lowest.
Finally, I am not a parent but I can't help but believe that requiring children to Wear life jackets
for two more years can only help ensure a lifelong pattern of safe use on the water. PFDs save lives. I have no statistics regarding the age of people who drowned. However, the Coast Guard's
2023 Recreational Boating Statistics identified 377 deaths due to drowning, the largest cause of
fatal boating accidents where the cause of death was known (75%): "Of those drowning victims with reported life jacket usage, 87% were not wearing a life jacket." 3
Thank you for your time and I hope to be able to answer any questions you have.

As a lifelong coastal Maine recreational boater and supporter safe boating education I am writing to support LD 1042 - An Act to Require a Person Operating a Watercraft for Recreational Purposes to Ensure all Passengers Under 13 Years of Age Wear Coast Guard Approved Personal Flotation Devices (PFD). I have struggled trying to explain to family and friends why, in Maine, there are inconsistencies in the regulations that apply to the wearing of a PFD by children between the ages of 12 and 13. I strongly support this bill. I appreciate your time and consideration in this effort to make our young people not only safer on the water, but to also give them confidence that logic and reason are used to enact our laws and regulations.

DIFW Rule requires children 10 years of age or younger wear a life jacket. Additionally, DIFW has broad outreach and educational campaigns encouraging people to wear PFDs

In Maine the Department of Marine Resources Marine Patrol enforces boating law in the territorial waters, and Maine Warden Service enforces boating law in inland waters. The
USCG enforces the state's law on mandatory PFD requirements when in state waters
because the state law takes precedence.

Testimony oflim Williams in favor of
LD 1042, An Act to Require a Person Operating a Watercraft for Recreational Purposes to Ensure All Passengers Under 1 3 Years of Age to Wear Coast Guard Approved Personal Flotation Devices
Before the Joint Standing Committee on Inland Fisheries and Wildlife
Good morning, Senator Baldacci, Representative Roberts and members of the
Inland Fisheries and Wildlife Committee, my name is Jim Williams. I reside on the New Meadows River, east Casco Bay in the Town of West Bath. I am a long-time recreational boater, hold a USCG Masters "Captains" License, am a Master Maine Guide and an
instructorfor the United States Power Squadron.
First, I wanted to talk about theterms used to describe the age at which a Personal
Flotation device (PFD) or Life Jacket must be worn. Some States say under age 13 and some say age 12 & under or 12 & younger. The term the Coast Guard uses is "Under 13" and LD 1042 uses "have not attained the age of 13". They all mean the same thing.
IFW Rule 13.05 now requires children aged 10 & under to wear a life jacket while on the water. LD 1042 requires 11 & 12 year-olds to also wear a life jacket. "Under 13" is the
age the Coast Guard uses. "Under 13" is also what % (three fourths) of the U.S. coastal
states (including D.C.) use and require. (See map on Page 2).
Life Jackets today are not the bulky uncomfortable PFD's of the past. They are
lightweight, come in many sizes, are reasonably priced, are available in inflatable or noninflatable versions and have many variations of colors and themes. Life Jackets must be on board the boat anyway, we are just asking that children wear them until they are 13 years
old.
Passage of this bill will help protect children for an additional two years while
recreationally boating. Odds are much greater that a child will survive a sinking, accident,
or capsize if a life jacket is being worn. Drowning is the leading cause (75%) of deaths
while boating and in 87% of drowning deaths a life jacket was not being worn. It just makes
sense to follow the Coast Guard's lead and protect our children for another 2 years. And there is no added cost to the State or the boater!
I urge you to support the passage of this legislation. Thank you for this opportunity to speak before you today. |'d be pleased to answer any questions from the Committee.
Respectfully,
Jim Williams
West Bath, Maine

Subject: Testimony supporting LD 1042 - An Act to Require a Person Operating a Watercraft for Recreational Purposes to Ensure all Passengers Under 13 Years of Age Wear Coast Guard Approved Personal Flotation Devices.
It is my pleasure, as Commander of the Wawenock Sail and Power Squadron, to write in support of LD 1042. The Wawenock Sail and Power Squadron, also known as America's Boating Club of Mid Coast Maine, is a non-profit organization dedicated to boating safety and education. Our goal is to promote safe boating through education. In our classes, we stress the importance of always wearing a personal flotation device (PFD) for all ages. Boating accidents happen quickly, without time to don a PFD. The leading cause of fatalities on the water is drowning and it is often preventable. Studies reveal that the vast majority of drowning victims were not wearing a life jacket at the time of the accident. Personal flotation devices are a simple yet life-saving measure.
Maine is one of the few states that allows 11- and 12-year-olds to ride in a boat without wearing a personal flotation device. Maine has over 116,000 registered boats, not including kayaks, paddleboards, canoes, dinghies, and rowboats. LD 1042 would bring Maine into conformance with the U.S. Coast Guard (USCG) Regulations requiring children under age 13 to wear a PFD. The law would protect children another two years while recreationally boating in Maine. It is ironic that Maine, with all its lakes, streams, and coastline, is more lenient than the USCG.
We, at the Wawenock Squadron, strongly support this bill. We appreciate your time and consideration in this important way to make our children safer on the water.
Sincerely yours,
Sharon L. Steele
